images.title: Why AB bisects XY at a right angle
images.purpose: Show the kite AXBY with diagonal AB meeting XY at O, the equal sides marked, and the right angle at O.
images.composition: A kite shape centred in the frame, A at the top, B at the bottom, X at the left, Y at the right.
exact_structure: Points A (top), B (bottom), X (left) and Y (right), each a small dark dot with its label.
Segments AX and AY in teal (#0072B2), each with one tick mark; segments BX and BY in amber (#E69F00), each with two tick marks.
A vertical dark line from A to B and a horizontal dark segment from X to Y, crossing at point O, labelled O.
OX and OY each carry a small reddish purple (#CC79A7) single bar mark showing they are equal.
A small square right angle mark at O between OA and OY.
The triangle AOX is lightly shaded teal (#0072B2) and the triangle AOY lightly shaded amber (#E69F00).
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: SSS then SAS show that AB cuts XY in half at a right angle.
images.description: Show the kite AXBY with diagonal AB meeting XY at O, the equal sides marked, and the right angle at O.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.

image_decisions.why: The congruent triangles must be seen side by side to follow the SSS then SAS argument.
